body:
#2058 (BUG-1565) APPROVED at 4d1e8ffd8068 — AND THE BREAK IT FIXES CAME
THROUGH MY REVIEW.

open_pr_for_same_spec_defers_auto_bump was added by #2040, which I approved at
66e1187377. I confirmed the ungated `use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;`
was present in that exact sha, at line 260.

I reviewed that PR closely on its LOGIC — the forge-kind distinction, the fake
gh's argv assertions, the opposite-direction control — and never once asked
whether the new test code could COMPILE on a non-Linux target. In a repo whose
PR CI is Linux-only BY DESIGN, with an open spec about portability defects
arriving at roughly the rate we merge. And the correct `#[cfg(unix)]` form
already existed about 2000 lines below IN THE SAME FILE.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A FAILING TEST, which they state and I want carried:
a compile failure takes the whole aida-cli-lib test target with it, so every
other test on that leg stops reporting. A failing test costs one signal; this
cost all of them. That is also why the two halves are both needed —
`#[cfg(unix)]` for the target to COMPILE, and `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore)]`
because a shebang fake gh is not executable there. AN IGNORED TEST STILL HAS
TO COMPILE, so the ignore alone would not have helped.

I REPRODUCED THEIR ENUMERATION INDEPENDENTLY, because it is the claim most
likely to be waved through:

    naive grep, tree-wide          I counted 64 (they report 14)
    diff from 84a7ea68a0, the last Windows-GREEN commit:
       3 unix usages added, 2 preceded by #[cfg(unix)], 1 NOT

Exactly their number. And their METHOD is the right one: the population is not
"every unix usage in the tree", it is "usages added since the last commit
Windows provably compiled" — everything older is gated somewhere the grep's
lookback cannot see. That is the same correction as counting by test rather
than assertion, and as breaking a total down before quoting it.

THEY ALSO BUILT A WORKING INSTRUMENT WHEN THE REPO'S COULD NOT FIRE.
`cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` dies in ring's build script —
the documented foreign-C limitation — so they tested the RULE in isolation
with a file containing only the import, both targets, both directions. That is
the right move against a known-broken detector, and the same shape as running
a gate against a known instance instead of trusting its claim to fire.

THE PRACTICE CHANGE, recorded on the verdict so it is not an apology: ON ANY
PR ADDING RUST CODE, GREP THE ADDED LINES FOR std::os::unix / std::os::windows
AND CONFIRM EACH IS INSIDE A CFG GATE. One grep over the diff, no build, and
it would have caught this in the review that let it through. The general form
is that this repo's PR CI cannot see portability BY DESIGN, so portability is
a REVIEWER obligation here — and I had been treating the nightly as the thing
that catches it, which is exactly the one-day-late loop BUG-1556 describes.
I was relying on the instrument that spec exists to say is too slow.

One note for the merge: the required check is Linux-only and CANNOT verify
this fix — Linux compiled fine before it. The evidence is their two-target
reproduction; the confirming signal is the next cross-platform run's Windows
leg REACHING the test phase rather than dying at compile.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2058 approved - and the Windows build break it fixes came through MY review of #2040. Ungated unix import was in the sha I approved; correct pattern was 2000 lines below in the same file
